title: SoftBank seeks $100bn from Gulf investors to expand AI bet
source_used: Financial Times report as relayed by Reuters on CNA (ft.com blocked, 403)
key_facts: SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son is seeking up to $100 billion from Gulf investors for a new wave of AI investments, the FT reported on Friday 9 Oct 2026, citing people familiar.
Son has held talks in recent weeks with senior figures, including in the United Arab Emirates.
Proceeds would set up a fund that acquires companies and improves their operations using AI and other advanced technologies, per the report.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report; SoftBank did not respond to a request for comment.
SoftBank announced last week it had completed its $30 billion investment in OpenAI.
SoftBank raised $11.1 billion last month in the largest high-yield corporate bond sale globally, to fund its OpenAI bet.
quote_evidence: Son has held discussions in recent weeks with senior figures, including in the United Arab Emirates, about the potential fundraising, the report said.
Reuters couldn't immediately verify the report.

The Japanese investment conglomerate would use the proceeds to establish a fund that would acquire companies and improve their operations using AI and other advanced technologies, according to the report.
why_it_matters_hint: A reported attempt to raise up to $100 billion shows how much outside money the AI build-out is drawing; nothing is agreed.
notes: FT page blocked (403, paywall). Text read via Reuters on CNA, which credits the FT as first reporter. Single-source report from unnamed people; Reuters could not verify.
